boundary_rationale: The row opens at 9:24 with the appeal Οὐκ οἴδατε (rp:1Cor.9.24) and the direct charge Οὕτως τρέχετε (rp:1Cor.9.24), which move from Paul's conduct to the readers. The same appeal stands at 9:13 as well (MEASURED, script gen_w3: 2 RP verses in 1Cor 8:1-11:1), so here it marks a turn together with the change of addressee. Behind the seam the summary Τοῦτο δὲ ποιῶ διὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον (rp:1Cor.9.23) closes the renunciation. The row closes at 9:27 on the fear of disqualification, ἀδόκιμος γένωμαι (rp:1Cor.9.27). Across the seam Οὐ θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί (rp:1Cor.10.1) opens the Israel example with a disclosure formula and vocative. SBLGNT reads ⸀γὰρ (sbl:1Cor.10.1) at that point, which ties 10:1 back to the self-discipline warning. Typing as example is held open against an exhortation reading. Here the seam itself is in doubt as well as the typing, because merges across 9:23/9:24 and across 9:27/10:1 are both weighed against it.

boundary_rationale: The row opens at 10:14 with Διόπερ, ἀγαπητοί μου, φεύγετε ἀπὸ τῆς εἰδωλολατρείας (rp:1Cor.10.14), an inference particle, a vocative and an imperative that turn the Israel example into a direct charge. The RP pilcrow at 10:14 informs and does not decide. SBLGNT spells the noun εἰδωλολατρίας (sbl:1Cor.10.14), and there is no SBL sign at 10:14. Behind the seam the assurance πιστὸς δὲ ὁ θεός (rp:1Cor.10.13) closes the Israel example. The cup and bread argument of 10:15-10:18 supports the charge, and Τί οὖν φημι (rp:1Cor.10.19) raises an objection inside the move. The row closes at 10:22 on the questions Ἢ παραζηλοῦμεν τὸν κύριον (rp:1Cor.10.22), and the RP pilcrow at 10:23 stands at the seam after it, where the slogan returns. Typing as exhortation is held open against an argument step, since 10:15-10:22 reasons more than it commands.

boundary_rationale: The row opens at 10:23 with the slogan and its reply, Πάντα μοι ἔξεστιν, ἀλλ’ οὐ πάντα συμφέρει (rp:1Cor.10.23), said twice in the verse, so slogan and response stay together in one unit. SBLGNT reads ⸀Πάντα ἔξεστιν (sbl:1Cor.10.23) in both halves, lacking the RP pronoun. The slogan extent contested here is whether the slogan is the words of permission alone or the clause with its reply, and either way no seam falls after 10:23. Behind the seam the questions Ἢ παραζηλοῦμεν τὸν κύριον (rp:1Cor.10.22) close the cup argument. The rule Μηδεὶς τὸ ἑαυτοῦ ζητείτω (rp:1Cor.10.24) and the market and dinner cases of 10:25-10:29 apply the reply, and the conscience vocabulary runs through 10:25, 10:27, 10:28 and 10:29 (MEASURED, script measure_w3: 7 verses book-wide). At 10:28 SBLGNT reads Τοῦτο ⸀ἱερόθυτόν ἐστιν (sbl:1Cor.10.28) for Τοῦτο εἰδωλόθυτόν ἐστιν (rp:1Cor.10.28) and lacks the RP clause Τοῦ γὰρ κυρίου ἡ γῆ καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς (rp:1Cor.10.28). At 10:29 the RP question ἵνα τί γὰρ (rp:1Cor.10.29) is read ἱνατί (sbl:1Cor.10.29) in SBLGNT, a spelling difference. The row closes at 10:30 on εὐχαριστῶ (rp:1Cor.10.30), a texture word, and Εἴτε οὖν (rp:1Cor.10.31) at 10:31 opens the summary.

boundary_rationale: The row opens at 10:31 with Εἴτε οὖν (rp:1Cor.10.31), which draws the conclusion of the food cases into the charge πάντα εἰς δόξαν θεοῦ ποιεῖτε (rp:1Cor.10.31). The inference pair stands in 2 verses book-wide (MEASURED, script measure_w3). Behind the seam εὐχαριστῶ (rp:1Cor.10.30) at 10:30 ends the dinner case. The charge widens at 10:32 to Jews, Greeks and τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ (rp:1Cor.10.32), and 10:33 grounds it in Paul's own practice, καθὼς κἀγὼ (rp:1Cor.10.33) and μὴ ζητῶν τὸ ἐμαυτοῦ συμφέρον (rp:1Cor.10.33). SBLGNT reads ⸀σύμφορον (sbl:1Cor.10.33) for the RP noun of that clause. The imitation charge Μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε (rp:1Cor.11.1) echoes 10:33 with καθὼς κἀγὼ χριστοῦ (rp:1Cor.11.1) (MEASURED, script measure_w3: the pair stands in 2 verses book-wide, 10:33 and 11:1, in RP and SBLGNT), so 11:1 closes the idol-food argument. Across the seam Ἐπαινῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς (rp:1Cor.11.2) opens a new subject with praise, and the RP pilcrow at 11:2 sits on that seam.
